# Project Plan: CodeMachine Landing Page

**Version:** 1.0
**Date:** 2025-11-22
**Generated By:** Codex (GPT-5)

<!-- anchor: project-overview -->
## 1. Project Overview

- **Goal:** Launch a premium Aura-themed landing page that convinces senior engineers to try the CodeMachine CLI by showcasing value, proof, and seamless install guidance.
- **High-Level Requirements Summary:**
  - Hero section must highlight the CLI value proposition, copyable `npm install -g codemachine` command, and a CTA directing visitors to the docs.
  - GitHub integration needs to surface live (or cached) star counts for `moazbuilds/CodeMachine-CLI` with graceful degradation to hardcoded copy.
  - Feature bento grid, glassmorphism simulation, and navigation must strictly follow the Aura visual system (noise, glows, Tailwind tokens, Inter/JetBrains fonts).
  - Documentation and GitHub links must open externally with security headers, while user journeys include clipboard confirmation and scroll-triggered reveals.
  - Responsiveness, accessibility, and error handling (clipboard fallback, disabled simulation on small screens) are non-negotiable cross-cutting behaviors.
- **Project Scale Classification:** Small — single-page SPA, deterministic content, 3 iterations, aligns with the Section 8.1 “Small” profile (3-5 tasks per iteration, limited components).
- **Key Assumptions:**
  - React 18 + Vite with Tailwind CSS is acceptable as the mandated frontend stack.
  - Hosting occurs on Vercel (primary) with Netlify parity; both support environment variables for optional GitHub tokens.
  - GitHub star fetches operate unauthenticated unless rate limits appear, at which point a read-only token can be injected.
  - Marketing/content updates flow through version-controlled TypeScript config files instead of CMS tooling.
  - Analytics hooks (e.g., PostHog) are optional but placeholders will be included to log copy/doc/GitHub interactions.

<!-- anchor: core-architecture -->
## 2. Core Architecture

- **Architectural Style:** Static Single-Page Application (React 18 + Vite) served from CDN edge nodes with progressive enhancement for clipboard, fetch, and animations.
- **Technology Stack:**
  - Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS Aura theme, Lucide icons, optional Framer Motion/IntersectionObserver utilities.
  - Backend: None (browser-only SPA), but GitHub REST v3 fetch runs client-side with optional authenticated headers.
  - Database: None; structured content lives in `src/content/*.ts`.
  - Messaging/Queues: Not required; async clipboard/fetch events handled inside hooks.
  - Deployment: Vercel (primary) or Netlify, Docker (node:20-alpine + pnpm) for CI parity.
  - Other Key Libraries/Tools: clsx/tailwind-merge utilities, PostHog `trackEvent` helper, Lighthouse/Playwright for verification.
- **Key Components/Services:** ExperienceShell, NavigationBar, HeroCommandPanel, VisualSimulationWindow, FeatureBentoGrid, IntegrationStatusBar, ContentConfigModule, ScrollRevealProvider, Observability utilities. *Component Diagram (Mermaid) planned in I1.T3.*
- **Data Model Overview:** Typed entities (HeroContent, FeatureCard, ExternalLink, StarMetric, VisualAsset, FeatureFlag) defined in `src/content` ensuring deterministic builds. *ERD (PlantUML) planned in I1.T2.*
- **API Contract Style:** RESTful GET to `https://api.github.com/repos/moazbuilds/CodeMachine-CLI`; contract captured via Markdown mini-spec. *Initial GitHub Integration Spec (Markdown) planned in I2.T3.*
- **Communication Patterns:** Components interact via props/context; hooks mediate clipboard and GitHub states, events logged through shared analytics helper. *Sequence Diagram (PlantUML) planned in I2.T2 to illustrate journeys.*

## 3. Directory Structure

- **Root Directory:** `codemachine-landing/`
- **Structure Definition:**
  ~~~
  codemachine-landing/
  ├── src/
  │   ├── components/
  │   │   ├── ExperienceShell/
  │   │   ├── HeroCommandPanel/
  │   │   ├── VisualSimulationWindow/
  │   │   ├── FeatureBentoGrid/
  │   │   └── IntegrationStatusBar/
  │   ├── content/           # Typed data models (HeroContent, FeatureCard, links, flags)
  │   ├── hooks/             # useClipboardCommand, useGitHubStars, useScrollReveal
  │   ├── styles/            # tailwind.css entry, noise/glow helpers
  │   └── lib/               # analytics helper, fetch utilities
  ├── public/                # Static assets (noise texture fallback, mobile screenshot)
  ├── docs/
  │   ├── diagrams/          # Mermaid/PlantUML sources for component, ERD, sequence views
  │   └── adr/               # Decision records and verification checklist
  ├── api/                   # Markdown specs for external integrations (GitHub fetch)
  ├── tests/
  │   ├── e2e/               # Playwright smoke scripts for clipboard, docs link, GitHub badge
  │   └── unit/              # Vitest specs for hooks/utilities
  ├── .vscode/               # Recommended workspace settings (optional)
  ├── Dockerfile             # node:20-alpine parity build
  ├── package.json           # pnpm-based dependencies and scripts
  ├── tailwind.config.ts     # Aura theme tokens, fonts, animations
  ├── vite.config.ts         # Vite bundler configuration
  └── README.md              # Project overview, setup, deployment, and flag instructions
  ~~~
  Key directories ensure documentation artifacts (`docs/diagrams`, `api/`) live beside source so autonomous agents can edit diagrams/specs without touching runtime code.

<!-- anchor: directives-strict-process -->
## 4. DIRECTIVES & STRICT PROCESS

- **Command Discipline:** Agents must avoid exploratory shell usage (e.g., `ls`) and rely on targeted actions; scripts should only touch files declared in their tasks to keep deltas focused.
- **Single-Write Policy:** Any generated artifact (Markdown, code, diagram) must be fully composed in-memory and written via one atomic redirect to honor the project’s deterministic build philosophy.
- **Validation Hooks:** After writing, agents run one-line Python or lightweight tooling to confirm file existence and rough length before moving on, preventing partial outputs.
- **Iteration Scope Guardrails:** Each iteration confines work to the directories listed in its tasks, reducing merge conflicts and keeping testing responsibilities near the code they affect.
- **Traceability:** Every artifact and feature change must reference the relevant requirement/journey so reviewers can verify compliance quickly; anchors and manifest entries are mandatory for lookup.
